title: Choosing between to work and working after the verb in front

teach.can_do: I can pick the right shape, to do or doing, for the verbs I use most often.
teach.why_it_matters: The sentence still makes sense when this is wrong, so nobody stops you. It just leaks a small error through every paragraph you write.
teach.meaning: Most of the time this carries no meaning at all. The verb standing in front reaches for one shape or the other, and which one it reaches for is a fact about that verb rather than a fact about the world. Enjoy takes doing. Decide takes to do. Nothing about enjoying is longer or less finished than deciding. So the verb and its shape are learned together, as one piece, the way the word itself was learned.

form.pattern: verb + to + base verb   |   verb + verb-ing
notes: Reaches for to: decide, want, hope, plan, agree, offer, refuse, learn, manage, afford, promise, seem, tend, fail, expect
Reaches for -ing: enjoy, avoid, finish, suggest, mind, keep, practise, consider, risk, deny, admit, involve, imagine, delay
Takes either, with no change of meaning: begin, start, continue, prefer, like, hate, love
There is no third list to work out. A verb that is not in one of the first two has to be looked up once and then stored
form.negative: The word not goes in front of the shape, never inside it: we decided not to renew the contract; she admitted not checking the figures.
form.question: Ask the verb, not the sentence: what does this verb take?

left.text: decided to move, agreed to pay, managed to finish, refused to sign

right.text: avoided moving, suggested paying, finished writing, denied signing

spec.caption: Two piles, and no rule running between them. The verb on the left of the gap tells you which pile you are standing in.

worked_example.sentence: The Marlow depot managed to cut its fuel bill without losing a single route.
worked_example.why_this_form: Manage is one of the verbs that arrives with to already attached, the way depend arrives with on. The choice was made by the word manage, not by the situation.
worked_example.what_the_other_would_mean: Managed cutting means nothing at all. That is the useful half of this point: the wrong shape here is not a different meaning, it is no meaning.

notice_set.sentence: The council avoided closing the Marlow library.
notice_set.question: Did the library close?
notice_set.why: Avoid says the thing was kept from happening, and the verb after avoid always turns up in the -ing shape.

notice_set.sentence: The crew managed to repair the pump before the tide turned.
notice_set.question: Was the pump repaired?
notice_set.why: Manage says the hard thing was actually done. Manage always takes to, whatever the sentence is about.

notice_set.sentence: Our neighbours have offered to drive us to the station.
notice_set.question: Have they driven you to the station yet?
notice_set.why: An offer points forward, so nothing has happened yet. Offer is one of the to verbs.

notice_set.sentence: She kept apologising for the delay.
notice_set.question: How many times did she apologise?
notice_set.why: Keep says the action came round again and again, and keep is one of the -ing verbs.

notice_set.sentence: The firm denied causing any lasting damage to the river.
notice_set.question: Does the firm say it damaged the river?
notice_set.why: Deny pushes the thing away from the speaker, and deny takes the -ing shape every time.

notice_set.sentence: We cannot afford to lose another driver this winter.
notice_set.question: Has a driver left this winter?
notice_set.why: The sentence is about what would be too costly, not about what has happened. Afford is a to verb.

discovery.prompt: Every sentence below is correct English. Try to find the rule that puts a sentence in the left column rather than the right one.
pairs: They enjoy walking to work.
They want to walk to work.
We finished repairing the roof.
We agreed to repair the roof.
He avoided answering the question.
He refused to answer the question.

candidate_rules.text: There is no rule to find. The verb on the left of the gap belongs to a list, and the list is learned rather than worked out.
Verbs about liking or disliking something take the -ing shape.
The -ing shape is used when the action goes on for longer.

teach.rule_line: Ask the verb in front, not the sentence. Store each verb with its shape attached.
teach.false_rule: That -ing here means a longer or unfinished action. It does not. Finish takes -ing, and finishing is exactly what is over.

errors.wrong: The council suggested to build a second footbridge.
errors.right: The council suggested building a second footbridge.
errors.why_it_happens: Suggest means roughly what advise and recommend mean, and those feel like to verbs, so to is supplied by analogy. Meaning is doing the choosing here, and meaning has no vote.
errors.smallest_fix: Change one word: to build becomes building.

errors.wrong: We are considering to move the depot to Verdon.
errors.right: We are considering moving the depot to Verdon.
errors.why_it_happens: Consider points at something not yet done, and a not-yet action feels as though it should take the forward-looking to shape. Consider simply refuses it.
errors.smallest_fix: Change one word: to move becomes moving.

errors.wrong: She enjoys to cycle along the towpath at the weekend.
errors.right: She enjoys cycling along the towpath at the weekend.
errors.why_it_happens: To do is the shape a learner meets first, so it becomes the default filling for every gap. Enjoy is one of the commonest verbs that will not take it.
errors.smallest_fix: Change one word: to cycle becomes cycling.

errors.wrong: They decided to moving the market to Tuesdays.
errors.right: They decided to move the market to Tuesdays.
errors.why_it_happens: Both shapes have been half-learned and both arrive at once. It is the signature of a chunk that was never stored whole, only as two loose pieces.
errors.smallest_fix: Delete three letters: moving becomes move.

pays_in.note: Every policy sentence has one verb sitting on top of another.
pays_in.model: Councils that plan to cut bus subsidies rarely consider replacing them with anything.

pays_in.note: A two-minute answer is a chain of verbs following verbs.
pays_in.model: I kept going back because I enjoyed working with people who had done the job for years.

pays_in.note: Whether the second action happened is carried by the first verb.
pays_in.model: The company denied withholding the survey results for eight months.

used_in.quote: Both sides of this essay are built from verbs like plan, expect, avoid and involve, each dragging its own shape behind it.
Saying what you enjoy, what you have decided and what you keep doing uses three different shapes in one answer.

payload.sentence: My manager has offered to swap my Friday shift.
payload.question: Has the shift been swapped?

feedback.why_key: An offer is something put on the table and not yet taken up. Offer is one of the verbs that arrives with to attached.
feedback.feed_forward: Read the first verb for what happened, and take its shape as given.

payload.sentence: The report avoided naming the firm responsible for the spill.
payload.question: Does the report name the firm?

feedback.why_key: Avoid says the naming was kept from happening. The -ing shape after it is not adding anything; avoid always takes it.
feedback.feed_forward: Let the first verb tell you what happened, not the shape of the second.

payload.context: From a paragraph about a college trying to save money.
payload.sentence: The college suggested to reduce the number of evening classes.
reasons: suggest takes the -ing shape, not to
the sentence needs a person after suggested
reduce is the wrong verb here
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: Suggest sits in the -ing pile. Nothing about the meaning of this sentence is wrong, which is exactly why the error survives so long.
feedback.feed_forward: Check suggest against the list before you write the second verb.

payload.context: From a letter about the last bus out of Verdon.
payload.stem: Passengers who miss it cannot afford ___ (wait) an hour for a taxi.

expected: to wait

feedback.why_key: Afford is a to verb, and it stays a to verb after cannot. The negative changes nothing about the shape.
feedback.feed_forward: Look past the negative to the verb that owns the shape.

payload.context: A cook talking about a busy Saturday.
payload.stem: I have finally finished ___ (plan) the menu for the weekend.

expected: planning

feedback.why_key: Finish sits in the -ing pile. The planning is over, so if -ing meant an unfinished action this sentence could not exist.
feedback.feed_forward: Store finish and its -ing shape as one chunk.

payload.context: From a maintenance note on the Verdon sensor trial.
payload.stem: The team keeps ___ (find) the same fault, and has agreed ___ (replace) the whole batch.

expected: finding, to replace
finding to replace

feedback.why_key: One sentence, two verbs, two different piles. Keep takes -ing and agree takes to, and neither choice is about the meaning.
feedback.feed_forward: Handle each verb separately; the sentence has no single setting.

payload.given: The landlord will not repair the boiler. He has said so twice.
payload.instruction: Write it as one sentence that starts with the landlord and uses refuse.

expected: to repair the boiler
to repair the boiler twice
twice to repair the boiler

feedback.why_key: Refuse belongs to the to pile, and it stays there whatever tense is wrapped round it.
feedback.feed_forward: Fix the shape from the verb, then worry about the tense.

payload.context: Build one sentence about a delay to the Ashfield recycling scheme.

expected: the council has postponed replacing the recycling bins

feedback.why_key: Postpone takes the -ing shape, and that shape sits directly against the verb with nothing between them.
feedback.feed_forward: Put the second verb straight after the first, in the shape the first one wants.

payload.audio_text: They've agreed to look at it, but they keep putting the meeting off.

expected: they've agreed to look at it, but they keep putting the meeting off
they have agreed to look at it, but they keep putting the meeting off
theyve agreed to look at it but they keep putting the meeting off

feedback.why_key: In speech the to after agreed is almost swallowed. If you never hear it you will never write it, and the sentence will come out as agreed look.
feedback.feed_forward: Listen for the small unstressed to riding between the two verbs.

payload.sentence: Most students avoid to ask questions in a full lecture theatre.

expected: avoid asking

feedback.why_key: Avoid is in the -ing pile. Nothing in the sentence signals it, which is why this one has to be retrieved rather than reasoned out.
feedback.feed_forward: When the fix is a list fact, retrieve it; do not argue from meaning.

payload.context: Someone talking about their shifts at the hospital.
payload.sentence: I've decided cutting down on nights, but I don't mind to work weekends.
reasons: both verbs have taken the wrong shape
only the first verb has taken the wrong shape
only the second verb has taken the wrong shape
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: Decide belongs with to and mind belongs with -ing, so the sentence has them the wrong way round twice over.
feedback.feed_forward: Check each verb against its own pile before you move on.

payload.prompt_text: A town is about to start collecting food waste from every street. Write one sentence saying what households will have to stop doing and what the council has agreed to provide.

feedback.why_key: The prompt forces one verb from each pile into the same sentence, which is where the error normally appears.
feedback.feed_forward: Write the first verb, then ask it what shape it wants.

payload.prompt_text: Take the body paragraph you wrote on the four-day week. Rewrite two sentences so that each one has a verb sitting on top of another verb, and check both shapes before you stop. Three minutes.

feedback.why_key: Under time pressure the default shape wins, and the default shape is to. Two sentences is enough to catch that habit in the act.
feedback.feed_forward: On the reread, look only at pairs of verbs standing next to each other.

title: Putting the -ing shape after every preposition, with no exceptions

teach.can_do: I can put a verb after by, without, after, instead of or good at without stopping to think.
teach.why_it_matters: This is the one place in the whole area where a real rule exists, it never has exceptions, and it repairs a very common written error at the same time.
teach.meaning: A preposition is a word that expects a thing after it: after lunch, without a ticket, good at maths. When what follows is an action rather than a thing, English turns the action into a thing by adding -ing. That is all -ing is doing here. It is not saying the action is long, or repeated, or still running. It is the shape a verb wears when it has to stand where a noun would stand.

form.pattern: preposition + verb-ing
notes: Common ones: by, without, after, before, instead of, on, in, for, about, of, at, with, since, apart from
Despite and in spite of are prepositions, so they take -ing or a noun and never a full clause
A few phrases end in the word to and that to is a preposition: look forward to, object to, be used to, be committed to, in addition to. The verb after them is -ing
A preposition can never be followed by to plus the base verb. There is no sentence in English where it can
form.negative: The word not goes between the preposition and the -ing: she apologised for not telling us sooner.
form.question: Is the word in front of the gap a preposition? Then the question is already answered.

left.role: the word before the gap is a preposition
left.text: by / without / after / instead of / good at / look forward to

right.role: so the verb can only wear -ing
right.text: closing, saying, finishing, replacing, fixing, hearing

spec.caption: One arrow, no branches. This is the only part of the unit where knowing the rule is enough.

worked_example.sentence: The depot cut its emissions by replacing the two oldest vans.
worked_example.why_this_form: By is a preposition, so whatever follows it has to stand where a noun stands. Replacing is the verb replace wearing the shape that lets it do that.
worked_example.what_the_other_would_mean: By to replace has no meaning available to it. The preposition has asked for a thing and been handed something that cannot be one.

notice_set.sentence: They cut costs by closing the two smallest depots.
notice_set.question: How were the costs cut?
notice_set.why: By names the method, and the action that is the method turns up in the -ing shape because by needs a thing after it.

notice_set.sentence: She left the meeting without saying anything.
notice_set.question: Did she say anything?
notice_set.why: Without is a preposition, so the action it rules out arrives as saying rather than as to say.

notice_set.sentence: After finishing the river survey, the team drove back to Verdon.
notice_set.question: Which happened first?
notice_set.why: After puts one thing before the other, and the thing it puts first is an action in the -ing shape.

notice_set.sentence: The scheme went ahead in spite of costing twice the estimate.
notice_set.question: Did the scheme cost more than expected?
notice_set.why: In spite of is a preposition, so the cost comes in as a thing. This is why despite cannot be followed by a full clause.

notice_set.sentence: I am looking forward to hearing from the housing office.
notice_set.question: Has the housing office written back yet?
notice_set.why: The to in look forward to is a preposition, not the to of to do. That is why hearing and not hear follows it.

notice_set.sentence: He apologised for arriving forty minutes late.
notice_set.question: Did he arrive late?
notice_set.why: For is a preposition, so the thing being apologised for is an action wearing the -ing shape.

discovery.prompt: One of these columns is impossible English. Work out what the left-hand words have in common.
pairs: We saved money by cycling.
We saved money to cycle.
She went out without locking up.
She went out without to lock up.
I object to paying twice.
I object to pay twice.

candidate_rules.text: By, without and object to all end in a preposition, and a preposition can only be followed by -ing.
Short linking words like by and without take -ing.
When the sentence contains the word to, the verb goes in its base form.

teach.rule_line: If the word before the gap is a preposition, the verb after it must be -ing.
teach.false_rule: That the word to is always followed by the base verb. In look forward to, object to and be used to, to is a preposition.

errors.wrong: Despite the survey was finished on time, the report arrived in June.
errors.right: Despite finishing the survey on time, the report arrived in June.
errors.why_it_happens: Despite means what although means, so it inherits although's grammar. Nobody mentions that one is a preposition and the other joins clauses, and the meaning gives no clue.
errors.smallest_fix: Change one word: was finished becomes finishing, and the subject goes.

errors.wrong: I look forward to hear from you about the tenancy.
errors.right: I look forward to hearing from you about the tenancy.
errors.why_it_happens: The learner sees to and applies the only rule they have for it. The to in look forward to is a preposition and looks identical to the other one.
errors.smallest_fix: Add three letters: hear becomes hearing.

errors.wrong: The council reduced waste by to collect food scraps separately.
errors.right: The council reduced waste by collecting food scraps separately.
errors.why_it_happens: To do is the default shape for a second verb, and it goes in even after a preposition that has no room for it. The result is a shape English cannot read at all.
errors.smallest_fix: Delete one word and add three letters: by to collect becomes by collecting.

errors.wrong: She is used to work nights, so the shift does not bother her.
errors.right: She is used to working nights, so the shift does not bother her.
errors.why_it_happens: Be used to and used to look the same and are learned at the same time. One is a preposition phrase about being accustomed; the other is a past habit and takes the base verb.
errors.smallest_fix: Add three letters: work becomes working.

pays_in.note: Every sentence about method, cause or concession runs through a preposition.
pays_in.model: Cities have cut congestion by charging for road space rather than by widening it.

pays_in.note: The standard closing line of a formal letter turns on this rule.
pays_in.model: I look forward to receiving confirmation that the repairs have been booked.

pays_in.note: Explaining how something could be done needs by plus -ing.
pays_in.model: You could cut most of that waste just by planning the week's meals in advance.

pays_in.note: A concession clause built on despite compresses a whole claim.
pays_in.model: Despite falling steadily since 2016, the figure remains above the national average.

used_in.quote: Every solution sentence in this task is built on by plus an action, and the action has to be a thing before by will take it.

payload.sentence: We got the bill down by turning the heating off at night.
payload.question: What brought the bill down?

feedback.why_key: By points at the method, and the method is an action that has been turned into a thing so that by can hold it.
feedback.feed_forward: Read by as how, then expect an -ing straight after it.

payload.sentence: Despite cutting its staff by a third, the depot met every delivery slot.
payload.question: Did the depot lose staff?

feedback.why_key: Despite is a preposition, so the staff cut arrives as a thing. The sentence still asserts it happened.
feedback.feed_forward: Treat despite plus -ing as a fact the writer accepts.

payload.context: The last line of a letter to a letting agency.
payload.sentence: I look forward to hear from you before the end of the month.
reasons: the to in look forward to is a preposition, so it needs -ing
look forward is the wrong verb for a letter
the sentence needs a subject after hear
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: Two identical-looking words are doing different jobs. This to is the kind that ends a phrase, not the kind that starts a verb.
feedback.feed_forward: Ask whether the to belongs to the phrase in front of it.

payload.context: From a paragraph about a town-wide recycling trial.
payload.stem: Ashfield halved its landfill waste by ___ (sort) glass at the kerbside.

expected: sorting

feedback.why_key: By is a preposition and there is no second option. This is the one gap in the unit you can fill without knowing the verb.
feedback.feed_forward: Spot the preposition first; the shape follows automatically.

payload.context: Someone describing their commute since the tram opened.
payload.stem: I am used to ___ (stand) now, and I leave without ___ (check) the timetable.

expected: standing, checking
standing checking

feedback.why_key: Both gaps sit behind a preposition, and the to in am used to is one of them. Neither gap has a choice to make.
feedback.feed_forward: Check whether to belongs to a phrase before you treat it as an infinitive.

payload.given: Although the college raised its fees, applications went up.
payload.instruction: Rewrite it starting with despite, keeping the same meaning.

expected: raising its fees, applications went up
raising its fees, the college's applications went up
raising its fees applications went up

feedback.why_key: Despite cannot hold a clause, so the clause has to be squeezed into an -ing shape before it will fit.
feedback.feed_forward: Swap although for despite and the verb loses its subject and gains -ing.

payload.context: Build one sentence for a report on a small savings scheme.

expected: the fund grew without taking on any new risk

feedback.why_key: Without has to sit directly in front of the -ing shape. Nothing can come between a preposition and the thing it holds.
feedback.feed_forward: Keep the preposition and the -ing word next to each other.

payload.audio_text: We cut the waste right down by planning the week's meals before shopping.

expected: we cut the waste right down by planning the week's meals before shopping
we cut the waste right down by planning the weeks meals before shopping

feedback.why_key: Two prepositions and two -ing shapes in one short sentence. In speech the endings are light, and light is exactly what learners stop writing.
feedback.feed_forward: Write the -ing ending even when you barely hear it.

payload.sentence: Many households now rent tools instead of to buy them outright.

expected: instead of buying

feedback.why_key: Instead of ends in the preposition of, and of will not hold an infinitive. The fix is the ending, not the word.
feedback.feed_forward: Look at the last word before the gap, not the first.

payload.sentence: Despite the rent was rising every year, most tenants stayed in the district.

expected: despite rising rents
although the rent was rising
despite the rising rent
despite the rent rising

feedback.why_key: Despite is holding a full clause, which it cannot do. Either the clause shrinks to a thing or the word changes to one that takes clauses.
feedback.feed_forward: Decide which side to move: shrink the clause or swap the connector.

payload.context: Someone talking about training for a half marathon.
payload.sentence: I used to running before work, but now I go at lunchtime.
reasons: this used to is the past habit one, so it takes the base verb
used to always takes -ing
the sentence needs but replaced with and
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: Used to on its own is a past habit and takes run. It is only be used to, with a form of be in front, that ends in a preposition.
feedback.feed_forward: Look for a form of be before used to before you reach for -ing.

payload.prompt_text: Someone asks how an ordinary household could cut its water use. Answer in one sentence that begins with a method, using by.

feedback.why_key: By plus -ing is the fastest way to answer a how question, and it is available before you have decided how the sentence ends.
feedback.feed_forward: Open with by, then let the -ing word carry the idea.

payload.prompt_text: Go back to your food-waste answer. Rewrite one solution sentence so it names the method with by plus -ing, and one concession sentence so it opens with despite plus -ing. Three minutes.

feedback.why_key: Despite plus a full clause is the error that survives longest, because it only appears when the sentence is long enough to forget how it started.
feedback.feed_forward: After writing despite, check that no subject follows it.

title: Building a sentence around the thing something was done to

point_json.grammar_name: The passive: what it does to a sentence

pays_in.note: Process and map answers are written almost entirely in this shape.
pays_in.model: Seawater is drawn into the plant through a screen at the intake.

pays_in.note: It lets a paragraph hold one topic in the subject slot throughout.
pays_in.model: The scheme was funded out of the transport budget rather than from reserves.

pays_in.note: Question stems flip a passage sentence into this shape and back again.
pays_in.model: The ridge was replanted after the fire of 2019.

teach.can_do: I can build a sentence around the thing something happened to, instead of around whoever did it.
teach.why_it_matters: Every process description and a great deal of academic prose is built this way. The form is small; what it does to a sentence is not.
teach.meaning: An ordinary English sentence starts with the doer: the council, the machine, the storm. Sometimes the doer is not what you want to talk about. This shape lets you move the thing that was affected to the front and make it the subject, so the sentence is now about that thing. The event itself does not change. What changes is where the reader's attention starts, and whether the doer appears in the sentence at all.

form.pattern: be + past participle
notes: be carries the time, exactly as it does anywhere else: is checked, was checked, will be checked
the past participle after it never changes shape
the doer, if you still want it, goes at the end after by
form.negative: be + not + past participle: the gates are not opened at night
form.question: Is the channel dredged every autumn?

left.text: the maintenance crew

right.text: the sluice gates

spec.caption: The right-hand box moves to the front of the sentence and takes the subject slot. The left-hand box steps back, or leaves altogether.

worked_example.sentence: The sluice gates are checked twice a day.
worked_example.why_this_form: The note is about the gates and their upkeep, not about which crew is holding the spanner, so the gates take the front of the sentence.
worked_example.what_the_other_would_mean: Two engineers check the sluice gates twice a day makes the engineers the subject, and a reader would then expect the next line to carry on about them.

notice_set.sentence: The old pumping station at Verdon was demolished last spring.
notice_set.question: Does the sentence tell you who knocked it down?
notice_set.why: Nobody is named. The building stands at the front because the building is what the sentence is about.

notice_set.sentence: A contractor from Norland knocked the pumping station down.
notice_set.question: Which does this sentence put first, the building or the people?
notice_set.why: The doer is in front, so a reader expects the next line to carry on about the contractor.

notice_set.sentence: Rainwater is collected on the roof and piped to a tank under the yard.
notice_set.question: Does it matter here who installed the pipes?
options: Yes, the sentence depends on it
No, the sentence works without it
notice_set.why: The interest is in where the water goes. Naming an installer would add a person nobody asked about.

notice_set.sentence: The proposal was rejected six weeks later.
notice_set.question: What is this sentence about?
options: The people who turned it down
notice_set.why: Putting the proposal in the subject slot keeps a paragraph about the proposal about the proposal.

notice_set.sentence: Two thousand trees were planted along the Ashfield ridge.
notice_set.question: Could you say who planted them from this sentence alone?
notice_set.why: The number and the place survive; the planters do not. That is the trade this shape makes.

notice_set.sentence: The storm brought down forty of the new trees.
notice_set.question: Does this sentence name what caused the damage?
notice_set.why: When the cause is the news, English puts it at the front and the sentence stays in its ordinary shape.

teach.rule_line: Decide what the sentence should be about, then put that first.
teach.false_rule: That this shape is a way of making writing sound clever. It is a way of choosing the subject. Any formality is a side effect of that choice.

errors.wrong: The pumping station demolished last spring.
errors.right: The pumping station was demolished last spring.
errors.why_it_happens: Demolished looks like a finished verb on its own, so nothing feels missing to the writer until a reader asks what the station demolished.
errors.smallest_fix: Insert one word: was.

errors.wrong: Forty of the young trees were broke in the storm.
errors.right: Forty of the young trees were broken in the storm.
errors.why_it_happens: Broke is the shape the learner uses in ordinary past sentences and it arrives first. The second form of an irregular verb is stored far more weakly than the first.
errors.smallest_fix: Change one word: broke becomes broken.

errors.wrong: The old mill was collapsed during the storm.
errors.right: The old mill collapsed during the storm.
errors.why_it_happens: The learner has decided this shape belongs in reports and applies it to every verb in one. Collapse has nothing to move to the front, because the mill is already the thing that came down.
errors.smallest_fix: Delete one word: was.

used_in.quote: Every stage of the heat-pump diagram is written in this shape, from the first sentence to the last.

payload.sentence: The reservoir above Verdon was drained over the summer.
payload.question: Does the sentence name anyone who did the draining?

feedback.why_key: The doer has been left out on purpose. What survives is the reservoir and what happened to it.
feedback.feed_forward: Check whether a doer is named before deciding what the sentence is about.

items.decision_cue: what happened to the depot yard

payload.context: Sam is describing what happened to the depot yard.
payload.sentence: The yard resurfaced in June.
reasons: the yard is shown as doing the work
the time named is wrong
this verb cannot take an object
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: As written, the yard is out there resurfacing something. One short word puts it back on the receiving end.
feedback.feed_forward: Add be when the subject is on the receiving end.

payload.context: From a note on the Verdon water works.
payload.stem: Silt ___ (remove) from the intake channel every autumn.

expected: is removed

feedback.why_key: Silt does not remove anything. It is what gets removed, so the sentence is built round it.
feedback.feed_forward: Match be to the time and leave the participle alone.

payload.context: Two neighbours are talking about the flats behind the station.
payload.stem: The whole block ___ (paint) last year and it still looks new.

expected: was painted

feedback.why_key: Last year fixes when it happened, and the block is on the receiving end, so was carries the date.
feedback.feed_forward: Put the time on be, never on the word after it.

payload.given: The council widened the approach road in March.
payload.instruction: Rewrite it so that the sentence is about the road.

expected: was widened in march
was widened by the council in march
was widened in march by the council
the approach road was widened in march

feedback.why_key: Moving the road to the front leaves nothing for it to do, so be steps in and the road becomes what the sentence reports on.
feedback.feed_forward: Put the affected thing first, then add be.

payload.context: A warden explaining the routine at the Verdon channel.

expected: every autumn the channel is dredged
the channel is dredged every autumn

feedback.why_key: Both orders are ordinary English. What neither of them does is tell you who runs the dredger.
feedback.feed_forward: Keep is and the participle together, wherever the time phrase goes.

payload.audio_text: The roof was checked before the tenants moved in.

expected: the roof was checked before the tenants moved in

feedback.why_key: Was is one unstressed syllable in the middle of a sentence, and it is the only thing marking the roof as the thing that got checked.
feedback.feed_forward: Listen for a short be in front of the -ed word.

payload.sentence: The intake screen cleaned every morning, and the debris is carted away.

expected: the intake screen is cleaned

feedback.why_key: The second half of the line shows the shape the first half is missing. Debris does not cart itself and screens do not clean themselves.
feedback.feed_forward: Read the two halves against each other before you submit.

payload.prompt_text: At a recycling plant, glass is sorted by colour before it goes into a crusher. Write one sentence about what happens to the glass. Do not mention the staff.

feedback.why_key: Nobody reading a process wants to meet the staff. Holding the glass in the subject slot is the whole register.
feedback.feed_forward: Start with the material, not with the plant.

payload.prompt_text: Take the first two stages of the dried pasta diagram and write them again as two sentences, keeping the wheat as the thing each sentence reports on. Three minutes.

feedback.why_key: Two stages in a row in one voice is what a process answer sounds like, and it is what a single sentence cannot show you.
feedback.feed_forward: Check that both sentences still open with the wheat.

title: Putting a sentence of that kind into whatever time I need

pays_in.note: A map answer moves between what stood there once and what stands there now.
pays_in.model: The old goods yard has been replaced by a park-and-ride.

pays_in.note: One topic can be held across several times inside a single paragraph.
pays_in.model: The charge was brought in during 2018 and has been increased twice.

pays_in.note: Travel announcements are almost all built this way, and the first word carries the news.
pays_in.model: The next two services have been cancelled.

teach.can_do: I can move this shape into any time, from what is happening now to what will happen next year.
teach.why_it_matters: There is one thing to learn here, not six. Learners who find this hard are finding be hard, and be is already known.
teach.meaning: Once you can build one sentence of this kind you can build all of them, because only one word does the work of placing it in time. Be moves exactly as it moves in an ordinary sentence, and the word after it sits still. So the difference between a job that is happening, a job that is finished and a job that is promised is carried entirely by the first word of the pair.

form.pattern: be, in any time you like, + past participle
notes: now, as a routine: is repaired, are repaired
in the past: was repaired, were repaired
happening as we speak: is being repaired
finished and still relevant: has been repaired
after will, must, can and to, be keeps its plain shape: will be repaired, to be repaired
form.negative: be + not + past participle: the line was not reopened until May
form.question: Has the line been reopened?

marks.label: was repaired
has been repaired
is being repaired
will be repaired

spec.caption: Only the first word travels. The word after it never leaves its place.

worked_example.sentence: The signal box at Sandmouth is being rebuilt.
worked_example.why_this_form: The work started and has not finished, and the speaker is standing in the middle of it, so being is what reports that.
worked_example.what_the_other_would_mean: Has been rebuilt would close the job and hand you a finished box, which is not what a passenger looking at the scaffolding would say.

notice_set.sentence: The signal box at Sandmouth is being rebuilt.
notice_set.question: Is the work finished?
notice_set.why: Being tells you the work is under way at the moment of speaking.

notice_set.sentence: The box at Sandmouth has been rebuilt.
notice_set.question: Is the work finished?
notice_set.why: Been closes the job and leaves the result standing in front of you.

notice_set.sentence: Three of the level crossings will be closed for good.
notice_set.question: Have those crossings shut yet?
notice_set.why: Will puts the whole event ahead of now, so nothing has happened so far.

notice_set.sentence: Freight was diverted through Brackenfield for eleven weeks.
notice_set.question: Is freight still going that way?
notice_set.why: Eleven weeks is named and closed, so the arrangement ended when they did.

notice_set.sentence: Tickets can be bought at the machine on platform two.
notice_set.question: Does the sentence say anybody has bought one?
notice_set.why: It reports what is possible, not what has happened.

teach.rule_line: Put the time on be and leave the word after it alone.
teach.false_rule: That each time has its own version to memorise. There is one version. Be does the moving, and you already know how be moves.

errors.wrong: The bridge has been rebuild since the flood.
errors.right: The bridge has been rebuilt since the flood.
errors.why_it_happens: Three words are stacked up and only the first two get any attention. After been, nothing is allowed to stay in its plain shape.
errors.smallest_fix: Change one word: rebuild becomes rebuilt.

errors.wrong: The branch line will reopened in the spring.
errors.right: The branch line will be reopened in the spring.
errors.why_it_happens: Will already feels like the whole of the future, so be looks like a spare part. It is the part that puts the line on the receiving end.
errors.smallest_fix: Insert one word: be.

errors.wrong: The depot was extended in 2019. New sidings are laid the following winter.
errors.right: The depot was extended in 2019. New sidings were laid the following winter.
errors.why_it_happens: The shape stays identical across the two sentences, so the writer stops noticing that the time has to be carried across as well.
errors.smallest_fix: Swap one form: are becomes were.

used_in.quote: Every change between the two maps is reported in this shape, and only the first word of the pair changes.

payload.sentence: The Ashfield line has been closed since the landslip.
payload.question: Are trains running on it today?

feedback.why_key: Been holds the closure against the present, so the line is still shut as you read.
feedback.feed_forward: Read the first word of the pair: it says where in time you are.

payload.context: Ravi is telling a friend about the flat he has just moved into.
payload.sentence: The kitchen was fitted last month, so everything in it is new.
reasons: the time is wrong
the word after was is wrong
be is missing
nothing wrong, it's fine

title: Choosing which of the two things in an event my sentence should be about

point_json.grammar_name: Active or passive: the five conditions

pays_in.note: A process or map answer lives or dies on this decision.
pays_in.model: The clay is pressed into moulds and then left to harden.

pays_in.note: It keeps one topic in the subject slot for the length of a paragraph.
pays_in.model: The levy was introduced without warning and has been raised twice since.

pays_in.note: Talking about what a society does needs a way to report effects without inventing a culprit.
pays_in.model: A lot of that work is done by volunteers now, which surprises people.

pays_in.note: A question stem often turns a passage sentence round to see whether you followed it.
pays_in.model: The eastern section was paid for out of a regional fund.

teach.can_do: I can work out which half of an event a sentence ought to be built around, and say why.
teach.why_it_matters: Both voices are correct English, so nothing here is about being allowed. What it is about is whether your paragraph holds together from one line to the next.
teach.meaning: Both shapes are correct, so the question is never which one is permitted. It is which of the two things in the event this sentence should be about, because English puts what a sentence is about at the front. If the doer is unknown, obvious, beside the point, very long, or simply not what this paragraph has been following, then the affected thing belongs at the front, and the passive is how you get it there.

form.pattern: be + past participle, with the doer dropped or moved to the end after by
notes: condition one: nobody knows or cares who did it
condition two: you are describing a made thing being made, not people at work
condition three: this sentence is about whatever the last sentence ended on
condition four: an institution is speaking and there is no I or we in it
condition five: the doer is a long heavy phrase that belongs at the end
if none of the five holds, the ordinary shape is shorter and clearer
form.negative: be + not + past participle: the tender was not awarded until June
form.question: Was the tender awarded in June?

ends: the affected thing is the news

worked_example.what_the_other_would_mean: The panel rejected it six weeks later swings the reader onto the panel for one line and then swings them back, which reads as a paragraph changing its mind.

candidate_rules.text: The version that settles begins with whatever the sentence before it was already about.
The version that settles is the one with no person in it.
The version that settles is the one with is, are or was in front of the -ed word.

teach.rule_line: Begin with whatever the last sentence left the reader holding.
teach.false_rule: That academic writing should be passive throughout. A wall of it is harder to read than a mixture, and each one has to earn its place.

contrast.question: Which of the two things in this event should the sentence be about?

fork.answer: The doer, because who did it is the news or the paragraph is following them
The affected thing, because who did it is unknown, taken for granted or already old news

a.text: The proposal reached the panel in January. The panel rejected it six weeks later.

contrast.wrong_choice_note: Taking the active here is not a grammar mistake and nobody will circle it. It moves the reader across to the panel for a single line and straight back, and a paragraph of that keeps changing its mind.

edge_case.text: Some style guides tell writers to delete every passive they find. That advice grew up in offices where writers used it to hide. In a description of a process, hiding the operator is the whole point. Follow the sentence, not the slogan.

title: Deciding whether to name the doer at the end, or to leave it out

point_json.grammar_name: by + agent: keep it or cut it

pays_in.note: Process answers drop the doer everywhere and keep the method every time.
pays_in.model: The sheets are trimmed by a rotary blade before they are stacked.

pays_in.note: A responsibility argument collapses the moment the doer goes missing.
pays_in.model: Air quality on the site is checked by a body with no stake in it.

pays_in.note: A stem that adds or removes a doer is testing whether you read the end of the sentence.
pays_in.model: The survey was carried out by a team from the university.

teach.can_do: I can decide whether the doer at the end of a sentence is worth its words.
teach.why_it_matters: Most learners either keep every doer or drop every doer. Deciding one sentence at a time is what separates a paragraph that informs from one that pads.
teach.meaning: Once the affected thing is at the front, the doer has two possible fates: it disappears, or it comes back at the end after by. Neither is the default. Keep it when the doer is specific, unexpected, or the reason anyone is reading the sentence. Cut it when the doer is people in general, or so obvious from the job that naming it tells the reader what they already assumed before they started.

form.pattern: be + past participle (+ by + the doer)
notes: the by phrase always comes after the participle, at the end of the clause
by can also mark an instrument or a means rather than a person: cut by machine, warmed by the sun
an instrument is information, so it is almost never the thing you cut
form.negative: the hall was not funded by the council but by a private trust
form.question: Who was the hall funded by?

rungs.text: The footbridge was rebuilt.

The footbridge was rebuilt by a charity nobody had heard of.

notice_set.why: The doer is not what a reader would have guessed, and that is exactly what makes it worth naming.

contrast.wrong_choice_note: Adding by the council to a sentence about a council building tells the reader what they assumed before they reached the verb. It costs three words and buys nothing, and a paragraph of those reads as padding rather than detail.

edge_case.text: By does not only introduce doers. Cut by machine, damaged by frost, warmed by the sun all name a means or a cause rather than a person, and those never come out, because they are the information.

options.why_this_means: That the building went back up and nothing about who paid is being reported.

options.text: was rebuilt by a trust set up by former traders
options.why_this_means: That the surprise is who paid, and the paragraph is about to explain them.

expected: was rebuilt by a trust set up by former traders

feedback.why_key: A visitor guide is written to tell you what you could not work out from the front of the building, and the traders are exactly that.
feedback.feed_forward: Keep the doer whenever it is the part a reader could not guess.

items.decision_cue: Every civic building is inspected each spring.

payload.context: A council maintenance schedule listing routine work. The line before reads: Every civic building is inspected each spring.
payload.stem: It ___ two years later.

options.why_this_means: That the building went back up and nothing about who paid is being reported.

options.text: was rebuilt by a trust set up by former traders
options.why_this_means: That the surprise is who paid, and the paragraph is about to explain them.

expected: was rebuilt

feedback.why_key: A schedule of routine work has no room for a story about traders. The document decides what counts as relevant, not the event.
feedback.feed_forward: Let the document you are writing decide what the reader needs.

items.decision_cue: The dried panels move on to the finishing bay.

payload.context: From a description of how ceramic panels are made. The line before reads: The dried panels move on to the finishing bay.
payload.stem: There they are trimmed ___.

options.why_this_means: That the method is what changes at this stage, and a reader following the process needs it.

options.text: by two workers on the late shift

expected: by a rotary blade

feedback.why_key: A process description follows the material through the machines. Who is on shift is a different document.

items.decision_cue: Labour is the largest single cost in the bay.

payload.context: From a note explaining why the finishing bay costs so much to run. The line before reads: Labour is the largest single cost in the bay.
payload.stem: There they are trimmed ___.

options.why_this_means: That the method is what changes at this stage, and a reader following the process needs it.

options.text: by two workers on the late shift

expected: by two workers on the late shift

feedback.why_key: The same stage, a different question. A note about wages needs the people; the blade is now the part nobody asked about.
feedback.feed_forward: Match the doer you keep to the question the text is answering.

payload.context: Two lines lifted from separate parts of one environmental report.
sentences: The estuary was polluted for eleven years.
The estuary was polluted for eleven years by a tannery upstream.
meanings: A problem is described and no one is answerable for it.
A problem is described and a named party can be asked about it.

feedback.why_key: The three words at the end are the difference between a weather report and an accusation.
feedback.feed_forward: Ask whether your sentence needs somebody to answer for it.

items.decision_cue: a housing association repainted last month

payload.context: Two tenants talking about a stairwell that a housing association repainted last month.
payload.stem: The stairs ___ in April.

options.why_this_means: That the state of the stairwell is the news and nobody is being credited or blamed.
That the association doing something at last is the news, and the paint is the evidence.

follow_up.question: Which one would you say if the conversation is about how slow the association has been?

feedback.why_key: Both are ordinary spoken English. One is about a stairwell and the other is about a landlord, and only you know which conversation you are in.
feedback.feed_forward: Pick the version that matches what you are complaining about.

items.decision_cue: a fire and the rebuilding that followed it

payload.context: From a paragraph about a fire and the rebuilding that followed it.
payload.sentence: The market hall was rebuilt by them after the fire of 2019.
reasons: the doer named at the end points at nobody
the time is wrong
the word after was is wrong
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: A doer with nothing behind it is worse than no doer at all, because the reader stops to look for the person and finds nobody.
feedback.feed_forward: Delete a doer you cannot name.

payload.prompt_text: Air quality on the Norland estate is checked every month, and the checking is done by a body with no connection to the operator. Write one sentence that makes the independence part of the news.

feedback.why_key: Independence only exists in the sentence if the doer is in it, so this is a case where the end of the sentence carries the argument.
feedback.feed_forward: Put the claim you want to defend into the by phrase.

payload.prompt_text: You are asked what has changed about the place you live in. Give a forty-five second answer with two sentences of this kind in it: one where the doer is left out and one where the doer is worth naming. Say why you kept the second.

feedback.why_key: One answer is the smallest space in which the decision has to be taken twice and taken differently.
